title: Web QA Automation
subtitle: A management decision backed by POC evidence
explain: Playwright for execution. Claude Code for broader suite authoring. Codex for focused vendor and CMS checks. Evidence limitations and pipeline next steps are explicit.

title: Playwright fits our complete web workflows
head: Decision point
Playwright
Selenium
Cypress
note: Recommendation: Playwright balances workflow coverage, evidence and setup.
explain: All three are viable. Playwright best matches RSA and Benefit workflows spanning forms, popups and connected data. Framework licence cost excludes hosting, labour and optional services. Cypress Cloud is optional and paid.

title: The fit comes from our project needs
head: Our workflow
Why Playwright fits
rows: Follow a journey across pages and popups
Select dependencies, fill fields and verify Save
Compare rendered values with service or CMS data
Replay failed steps with screenshots and traces
note: Choose for these capabilities and the work we need to test.
explain: This is a capability-based selection. We do not use existing implementation or avoiding a restart as the reason to choose Playwright. Database and CMS comparisons require a defined expected result and access.

title: Repeatable checks and clearer failures
head: Strong point
Business benefit
Cost boundary
rows: Run the same checks after changes
QA can see where the journey failed
Runner, AI and team time still cost
note: The benefit is reliable release evidence; savings have not been measured.
explain: No ROI or time-saving percentage has been established in this POC. Tool capability supports the recommendation; teams must still review business assertions, account access and data cleanup.

title: Recommend Claude Code for the broader web suite
head: Job
Recommended role
Evidence supporting it
note: This is a job-specific recommendation based on available POC evidence.
explain: Claude Code has the broader documented delivery for this job. This is not proof of universal superiority, lower cost or greater accuracy. Codex demonstrated a narrower but detailed vendor creation and CMS validation workflow.

title: The results support different strengths
head: Evidence
Claude Code / RSA
Codex / Benefit
note: Different tasks and scope: these numbers are not an equal-task competition.
explain: The RSA results are reported from the source POC, not rerun here. Benefit’s two passing executable tests are one vendor business check and one login setup. Nineteen value comparisons are field checks, not nineteen business cases. Full corrected BenefitDB/CMS comparison remains pending.

title: Confirm the AI choice with the same assignment
head: Measure
Fair comparison
rows: Same journeys, access and acceptance rules
Record corrections needed before QA accepts
Use the same known failures and expected results
Compare actual usage plus reviewer time
note: Proposed next step: a matched-task trial before claiming speed or cost superiority.
explain: This benchmark is a plan and has not been completed. Both tools should receive identical project access, test cases, environment, data and review criteria. Compare accepted outcomes rather than the number of generated tests.

title: Use each tool for a clear responsibility
head: Tool
Strength
Limit to manage
rows: Needs correct assertions and stable data
Skipped cases and QA review remain
note: Recommended combination: Playwright executes; AI helps author; QA owns acceptance.
explain: Evidence: reported Claude RSA suite 61 cases, 57 passes and 14 skips; saved local RSA subset six passes; saved Codex Benefit vendor flow plus login two passes and nineteen CMS checks. Authoring and execution have different responsibilities.

title: Benefit POC: saved vendor and visible details
note: Synthetic vendor 20415 · 19 rendered values matched CMS · full DB comparison pending.
explain: Saved evidence from 8 October 2026. The left image captures the successful creation toast. The right image shows the upper portion of vendor details. Vendor ID 20415 and CMS item d4b1c8e8-d8ac-415d-86eb-856391f9a531. This demonstrates save, detail display and nineteen CMS-rendered value comparisons. It does not prove every optional field persisted or full database parity.

title: The POC shows progress and specific next actions
head: Observed gap
Action
Why it matters
rows: Restore access and finish the check
Prove persistence as well as display
note: Resolve prerequisites, then expand the accepted test pack.
explain: A successful UI/CMS comparison is narrower than full end-to-end integration proof. Some earlier Benefit assumptions about disabled fields were corrected by selecting Thailand at the top right, English and reloading. Access expiry prevented completion of the corrected full DB comparison.

title: Coverage needs a confirmed baseline
note: “300 of 400” is unverified. Confirm that case pack before reporting 75%.
explain: The canonical RSA POC reports a catalogue of 449 cases across 22 sheets, 61 implemented cases and 388 not started. 61/449 is 13.6% implemented coverage of that reported catalogue. This is not passing coverage. No verified 300/400 inventory has been supplied.

title: Separate cases, executable tests and results
head: Measure
Recorded value
What it means
note: Report completed business scope and passing execution separately.
explain: A business case may produce multiple executable tests. Setup tests should not be presented as additional business coverage. The local RSA six-test saved result includes five functional tests and setup; the thirteen-test inventory includes twelve functional tests and setup.

title: The 14 reported skips have concrete prerequisites
head: Reason
Tests
What enables execution
rows: Approved accounts with the required roles
Test identities for the sign-in service
Controlled job data for the scenarios
note: A missing prerequisite does not establish that a scenario cannot be automated.
explain: These counts explain the fourteen reported RSA skips. They do not explain a supposed remaining one hundred cases. The 388 not-started catalogue cases need individual assessment; they are not all impossible. Source POC dated 8 October 2026.

title: Fully automate the digital checks we can observe
head: Scenario
Automation scope
Prerequisite
rows: Sign in and verify permitted actions
note: Full automation is possible within a defined digital scope and available access.
explain: Full means all assertions of a defined digital scenario can be checked. It does not imply every integration has been proven. Benefit’s corrected complete DB/CMS comparison remains pending.

title: Some journeys need automated and human evidence
head: Journey
Automated part
Remaining proof
note: Label these journeys as partial when the external outcome is not verified.
explain: A digital status update does not independently prove physical roadside service completion. Controlled integration checks can be automated; real external outcomes may require provider evidence or a human check.

title: Keep human judgement explicit
head: Human check
Why it remains
How to report it
rows: Depends on a person or protected challenge
Approved test path, otherwise manual step
Scope has not yet been reviewed
note: Classify each remaining case: full, partial, prerequisite-blocked or manual.
explain: MFA and CAPTCHA should not be bypassed. Approved test identities or test-environment paths may enable digital automation. These are scenario categories, not a verified breakdown of one hundred remaining cases.

title: Move from local proof to an unattended pilot
head: Phase
Deliverable
Acceptance evidence
rows: Case list, required count and owner
Actual hosted run and report link
Reliable evidence and agreed release gate
note: Proposed plan: prove one hosted pilot before expanding release controls.
explain: The POC contains a draft CodeBuild setup and local gate checks. No cloud QA run or deployed QA pipeline has been demonstrated. Ten unattended runs is a proposed acceptance target, not a completed result.

title: The local gate rejects incomplete success
head: Local check
Result
Management meaning
rows: Pass / fail / skip / empty / incomplete handled
A green subset cannot stand for the full pack
Saved focused pack met its required count
note: Local gate proof is complete; hosted execution is the next evidence milestone.
explain: Local validator rerun 9 October 2026 against saved results: complete passing run accepted; failed, skipped, empty and incomplete runs rejected. No browser rerun or cloud pipeline deployment was performed for this presentation.

title: The pilot needs an owner and evidence of recovery
head: Need
Owner / proof to agree
rows: Approved test access; predictable data and cleanup
Restricted reports, screenshots, traces and videos
Run ID and accessible results for the complete pack
Deliberate failure blocks the gate; corrected rerun passes
note: Use these checks to decide when the pipeline is ready for release use.
explain: Runner image, environment configuration, secrets, network access and cleanup need ownership. Evidence should avoid credentials and customer data. A hosted run ID, report link and demonstrated failure/recovery are needed before claiming pipeline readiness.

title: The management decision and next steps
head: Decision
Next action
rows: Use complete workflows and reportable evidence
Confirm with a matched-task trial; Codex for focused checks
Approve one inventory; resolve the 300 / 400 discrepancy
Assign a pilot owner and prove unattended execution
note: Proceed with a controlled web pilot and publish only evidenced results.
explain: Supporting project: https://github.com/bulubuloa/AS.APAC.AI.Workshop . Roadside-web is the published example. Benefit focused project is local and has not been published to that repository. The approved Confluence pages contain the supporting detail.
